Definition: relationship by blood or marriage; paternal or brotherly relationship. The mïṟ relationship is valid betweenpersonsbelongingtothetwomoeitiesalso(TöwfiɫyandṬoːrθasmoi- eties); mïṟ wïḍḍi ‘there is mïṟ’, mïṟ ill-ïyi ‘there is no mïṟ’, aθ mïṟ aṟsči ‘He/she knows the mïṟ’ (= knows whether we havemïṟ or not); a mox nïn-k in mïṟ-u? ‘What is the relationship between you and that boy?’ (< do you both have a mïṟ between yourselves?). Answers could be: 1. a mox en-k močin-oːɫ ïyi,̣ mïṟ oːx-ïyi ‘He is my cross-cousin (e.g. father’s sister son), there is no mïṟ.’ (so we can marry) (močin-oːɫ c̣ross-cousin), 2. en-k mïṟ ïyi, tanoṇ oyt ïyi ‘He has mïṟ relationship (with me), he becomes my elder brother’ (so we cannot marry) (tanoṇ‘elder-brother’, oyt ïyi ‘he becomes’), 3. en-k ïtwïḍ mïṟ ïyi ay oːɫ ‘Hẹ has elder mïṟ relationship with me (He is equivalent to my grandfather, paternal un- cle etc.)’ (so we cannot marry) (ïtwïḍ big), en-kn aːn-g-m mïṟ oːṛθi ‘Between him/her and I there is no mïṟ.’
